name: sen_sero

o_discriminators.name: A/D1 rfbS
o_discriminators.note: A (O:2) versus D1 (O:9): rfbS, whose paratose/tyvelose polymorphism is the only sequence difference between the two serogroups' rfb clusters

o_discriminators.name: D1/D2 wbaV
o_discriminators.note: D1 (O:9,12) versus D2 (O:9,46): wbaV, 7 SNPs apart and conserved across Enteritidis genomes; no D1 wzy reference exists and the wzx alleles differ by only 0.08 pp

o_discriminators.name: E1/E4 wbaP
o_discriminators.note: E1 (O:3,10) versus E4 (O:1,3,19): wbaP, the O-antigen initiating transferase, 1.22 pp apart; wzx/wzy cannot decide because SISTR's E1 wzx class contains O:1,3,19 references

o_subfactor.note: O:22/O:23 sub-factor discriminator (presence/absence of the O:22-specific and O:23-specific galE+glycosyltransferase blocks, which are ~62 % identical and therefore not alleles) and the Enteritidis Sdf I region, extracted from public-domain NCBI records.

special_checks.note: Sdf I detected: characteristic of commonly circulating Enteritidis
oafA absent/truncated: Typhimurium O5- variant (4,[5],12 antigen)
oafA absent/truncated: monophasic Typhimurium O5- variant
STM3356 (gntR) d-tartrate non-fermenting allele (dt-): Paratyphi B var. Java / typhoidal pathotype
STM3356 (gntR) d-tartrate fermenting allele (dt+): Paratyphi B var. L(+) tartrate+

naming_priority.note: C2-C3:r:l,w — the H1 spellings r and r,[i] are one antigen, and the two rows they key (Goldcoast, Brikama) are the same formula. Evidence: a reference laboratory's agglutination result was literally 'Goldcoast or Brikama' (PMC9150820, SAMN26764377 / SAMN26764405); PMC8552638 submitted its isolate A030_06/19 as Goldcoast with the same in-silico ambiguity; SISTR reports Goldcoast. Brikama has no public genome at all, so no sequence evidence can ever prefer it.

C2-C3:r:1,5 — same r/[i] spelling pair. Bovismorbificans is O:6,8,20 and Hindmarsh is O:8,20, but the O:6 factor has no marker in the rfb cluster (13 complete genomes, 3220 CDS clusters, no cluster splits the groups). Evidence: SISTR reports Bovismorbificans; SeqSero2's curated rename_dict maps Hindmarsh to Bovismorbificans (the WHO merge).

6,8,20:e,h:1,2 — a single formula key that literally carries two serovar names. Newport is the common serovar; SeqSero2's rename_dict maps Bardo to Newport and comments that Bardo is exceedingly rare.

unresolved: Salmonella subsp. enterica (no antigen set resolved)
